name: colibri
description: A hierarchical inference engine for frontier MoE models: hot experts on the GPU (CUDA, Vulkan), warm ones in RAM, cold ones streamed from NVMe. Written in C, runs on the hardware you already own.
one_liner: Software that lets you run enormous AI models on a regular gaming computer by keeping the parts it's using in memory and pulling the rest off your hard drive as needed.
buyer: A small AI startup or solo power-user who wants to run frontier-scale open models without paying for expensive cloud GPUs or buying a data-center card.
business_use_cases: A boutique AI consultancy offers clients 'run it on your own hardware' deployments of huge open-source models for data-sensitive work, using a single workstation instead of a cloud GPU bill.
A hobbyist AI YouTuber builds content around running and benchmarking frontier open models on consumer PCs, driving sponsorships and affiliate hardware sales.
A homelab/self-hosting enthusiast sells pre-configured mini-PCs set up to run specific large models for people who don't want to do the setup themselves.

money_ideas.idea: Sell pre-built or pre-configured hardware bundles tuned to run specific popular large models smoothly.
Paid setup and tuning service for companies wanting one specific huge model running affordably on their own servers.

steal_this: Build and sell a simple benchmarking/config dashboard that tells someone exactly which large models their specific PC can run well with colibri, and auto-generates the config.
